message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid on ELECTRIC_COMPANY in this auction.

p4 has already bid $160 and claimed that is their limit. They own WATER_WORKS and want the utility monopoly. I have $1170 in cash and no monopolies yet. I will likely drop out unless p4 bids significantly higher.

Denying p4 the utility monopoly would be strategically valuable. With both utilities, rent increases from roughly $28 to $70 per landing. This would hurt all opponents, including me.

A lone utility is weak without Water Works. I am weighing a $161 bid to force p4 to fold or continue. That would leave me with roughly $970 to $1009 in cash. Keeping the trade chip could let me swap Electric Company for cash or another needed property later.

I am checking which monopolies I still need. Mediterranean would complete the browns, but that set is weak. p2 owns St. Charles, so States and St. Charles are not viable for pinks. Ventnor and Marvin are unowned for yellows. p1 already has the orange monopoly with Vermont, St. James, and New York, which is dangerous because they can build houses.

p2 owns scattered properties including Illinois and St. Charles. p4 has two railroads plus the utility. I will not overpay for a utility.

The orange monopoly poses a larger threat than blocking p4's utility. A $161 bid would cost me $161 for a $150 property, but it would secure the trade chip and block their monopoly if p4 folds.

The denial value could be $50 to $150 or more depending on landings. I can sell the utility later for a profit if p4 gets desperate. A $161 bid is cheap enough to call p4's bluff. If they continue, I will likely cap my bid around $200 to $250.

I will bid $161 to pressure p4 into folding. I will not reveal my ceiling. If they continue, I will reassess next turn.
